title: 第三十四章 程家姐弟的酸意第三十三章 落网
slug: 诸天影视从四合院开始
content_zh:
叶晨推开家门的时候，客厅的灯还亮着，牛玲玲正从客房里出来，手里端着一只搪瓷盆，盆沿搭着一条毛巾，看见叶晨进来朝他嘘了一声，压低声音说道：
“小紫刚睡着，你走路轻点儿。”
叶晨换了拖鞋，往客房门口探头看了一眼，那孩子躺在铺着崭新格子床单的小床上，被子盖到下巴，小脸侧着压在一只嫩绿色的枕套上，呼吸均匀，嘴角还带着一点若有若无的弧度，像是梦见了什么让她安心的事儿。
床头的台灯被调到了最低一档，暖黄色的光晕罩在她脸上，把那颗小脑袋周围照出一圈模糊的轮廓。
袁山青站在客厅角落里，两手垂在身侧，脚上穿着一双牛玲玲刚给她翻出来的新棉拖鞋，蓝色的，鞋面上印着一只卡通小狗。
她整个人局促得不知道该往哪儿钻，像是怕自己多踩一脚地板，就会把什么东西弄脏似的。
牛玲玲放下搪瓷盆走过去，伸手拉住她的胳膊，也不问她愿不愿意，就直接把她带进了盥洗室。
作为一个成年人，牛玲玲自然是看出来这个孩子的局促和紧张，她语气轻松的说道：
“来，婶儿帮你洗洗头。你这一头汗，不洗洗睡不踏实。”
她打开热水器试了试水温，把花洒调到最温柔的一档，水雾腾起来的时候，卫生间里弥漫着一股好闻的香皂味。
袁山青被按在小板凳上，脖子上围了一条干毛巾，她低着头，热水从发梢淌下来的时候，肩膀微微颤了一下，但是没有躲开。
牛玲玲的动作很轻，手指穿过她被血和汗粘在一起的毛发，一点一点地把那些纠结在一起的发丝梳开。
袁山青的头发比她想象中要细要软，养得不怎么好，发尾有些枯黄分叉，被热水泡过之后，那股子灰扑扑的劲儿渐渐退了下去，露出一层暗哑的、原本的颜色。
牛玲玲挤了洗发水在掌心搓开，揉在她头皮上的时候，明显感受到那个孩子的肩膀在一点一点地往下松，从绷紧的弓弦终于变成了一截终于敢靠岸的木头。
水流冲过头顶的时候，袁山青的后脖梗完整地露了出来，暖黄色灯光底下，牛玲玲看清了她后颈那道旧疤，又被她撩开衣领的间隙里，瞥见了肩胛骨上一块指甲盖大小的、已经变成淡白色的圆形伤疤。
牛玲玲是开饭店的，每天接触到的都是社会上的三教九流，对于这样的疤痕她自然是不会陌生，这明显就是一块烟疤。
牛玲玲的脸色很难看，她甚至有了想杀人的冲动。在一个小女生身上，出现了一块烟疤，而且是在肩胛骨的位置上，用屁股想都猜得到，这肯定不是自己弄上去的，所以答案显而易见，一定是被袁勇那个畜牲给烫的。
她的手指停顿了一瞬，随即继续抚过她的发根，洗完了用干毛巾给她包上头发，又帮她擦干了脸颊和耳朵后面，每个动作都不急不缓，让人找不到躲闪的空隙。
“行了，去睡吧。”
牛玲玲帮女孩儿吹干头发后，拍了拍她的肩膀，把她带进客房，看着她在床边坐下来，替她掖好了被角，又指了指床头柜上放好的那杯水，柔声说道：

“要是不舒服了就喊婶儿，我就在隔壁屋，能听见。”
袁山青脸贴着那个嫩绿色的枕套，轻声说了一句：
“谢谢婶儿。”
她的声音闷在枕头里，含含糊糊的，像是一颗从很远的地方飞来的石子，终于落了地。
第二天早上六点，叶晨准时出门晨练。秋天的天亮得晚，这会儿外面还笼着一层灰蒙蒙的晨光，空气里带着露水的湿气和草叶被踩碎后散发出的青涩味道。
他沿着家属院外围跑了三圈，又在单杠上拉了几个引体向上，顺便拐到农贸市场门口那个早点摊买了油条、豆腐脑和两笼包子，用塑料袋装着拎回来的时候，楼下的那排梧桐树正好被初升的太阳照到树梢。
推门进屋的时候，客厅里弥漫着一股清甜的气息，李大海正坐在餐桌边看一份报纸，面前摆着一碟酱菜。
叶晨把早餐放下，刚要去叫牛玲玲出来吃饭，就听见客房里传来母亲牛玲玲的声音：
“李大海，你快帮我打个电话给程鹏飞，让他早上去单位挂个号，袁山青发烧了！”
程鹏飞也是倒了霉了，刚值完夜班，还没等睡踏实呢，就被牛玲玲一个电话叫醒。不过他可不敢有任何的怨言，尤其是在得知昨晚那个女孩儿身体出现不适的前提下。
叶晨把手里的早餐往餐桌上一搁，走到客房门口，隔着一道门问了一句：
“妈，她烧得厉害吗？”
牛玲玲的声音从里面传出来，带着一丝急促，但却不慌乱：
“滚烫的，整个人跟蒸过似的。李肆，你吃完饭赶紧去上学，顺便帮她跟老师请一天假，我跟你爸开车送她去医院看看。”
叶晨站在门外停顿了一下，没有立刻搭话。他靠在走廊的墙上，脑子里转了一下——疫苗后的正常反应，通常是接种后六到十二个小时开始出现，低烧、乏力、注射部位红肿，持续一天左右就会自行消退。
作为一名专业的医生，他当然知道这个，但他没说。他心里面很清楚，牛玲玲虽然自家就有个儿子，可是心里面却一直都希望家里再有个女孩儿，毕竟程家儿女双全的场面，让她一直都很羡慕。
content_en:
When Ye Chen opened the door, the light in the living room was still on. Niu Lingling was coming out of the guest room, holding an enamel basin with a towel on the edge. When she saw Ye Chen come in, she shushed him and said in a low voice:
"Xiao Zi just fell asleep, please walk more gently."
Ye Chen changed his slippers and peeked at the door of the guest room. The child was lying on a small bed covered with brand-new plaid sheets, with the quilt covering his chin. His little face was pressed sideways on a green pillowcase. He was breathing evenly, and there was a vague arc at the corner of his mouth, as if he had dreamed of something that reassured her.
The bedside table lamp was adjusted to the lowest setting, and a warm yellow halo shone on her face, illuminating a blurry outline around her little head.
Yuan Shanqing stood in the corner of the living room, with his hands hanging by his sides. On his feet, he was wearing a pair of new cotton slippers that Niu Lingling had just dug out for her. They were blue and had a cartoon puppy printed on them.
She was so cramped that she didn't know where to go, as if she was afraid that if she stepped on the floor one more time, she would stain something.
Niu Lingling put down the enamel basin and walked over, reached out and took her arm, and took her directly into the bathroom without asking her if she wanted to.
As an adult, Niu Lingling naturally saw the child's embarrassment and nervousness, and she said in a relaxed tone:
"Come, auntie, help you wash your hair. You're so sweaty, you won't be able to sleep well unless you wash it off."
She turned on the water heater, tested the water temperature, and adjusted the showerhead to the gentlest setting. When the water mist started to rise, the bathroom was filled with a pleasant scent of soap.
Yuan Shanqing was pressed on a small bench, with a dry towel wrapped around her neck. She lowered her head. When the hot water dripped from the ends of her hair, her shoulders trembled slightly, but she did not move away.
Niu Lingling moved very gently, running her fingers through her hair that was stuck together with blood and sweat, and combing out the tangled hair bit by bit.
Yuan Shanqing's hair was thinner and softer than she expected, and it wasn't well maintained. The ends of her hair were a little dry and yellow with split ends. After being soaked in hot water, the gray hair gradually receded, revealing a dull, original color.
Niu Lingling squeezed the shampoo into her palms and rubbed it into her scalp. When she rubbed it on her scalp, she could clearly feel that the child's shoulders were loosening little by little, from a taut bow string to a piece of wood that finally dared to touch the shore.
When the water rushed over her head, the back of Yuan Shanqing's neck was completely exposed. Under the warm yellow light, Niu Lingling could clearly see the old scar on the back of her neck. When she lifted up her collar, she caught a glimpse of a round scar on her shoulder blade that was about the size of a fingernail and had turned pale white.
Niu Lingling runs a restaurant, and she comes into contact with all kinds of people in society every day. Naturally, she is no stranger to scars like this. This is obviously a cigarette scar.
Niu Lingling's face was ugly, and she even had the urge to kill someone. On a little girl, a cigarette scar appeared on her body, and it was on the shoulder blade. You could guess it with your buttocks. It was definitely not caused by herself, so the answer was obvious. It must have been burned by that beast Yuan Yong.
Her fingers paused for a moment, and then continued to stroke the roots of her hair. After washing, she wrapped her hair with a dry towel, and wiped her cheeks and behind her ears. Every movement was not hasty or slow, leaving no room for dodge.
"Okay, go to bed."
After Niu Lingling helped the girl dry her hair, she patted her shoulder and took her into the guest room. She watched her sit down by the bed, tucked her into bed, pointed to the glass of water on the bedside table, and said softly:
"If you feel uncomfortable, call Auntie. I'm in the next room and can hear you."
Yuan Shanqing pressed his face against the tender green pillowcase and said softly:
"Thank you, auntie."
Her voice was muffled in the pillow, muffled, like a pebble flying from a far away place and finally falling.On the ground.
At six o'clock the next morning, Ye Chen went out for morning exercises on time. The autumn day dawned late, and now there was still a layer of gray morning light outside. The air was filled with the moisture of dew and the green smell of crushed grass blades.
He ran three times around the perimeter of his family's courtyard, did a few pull-ups on the horizontal bar, and then turned to the breakfast stall at the entrance of the farmer's market to buy fried dough sticks, tofu bread, and two steamed buns. When he brought them back in plastic bags, the row of sycamore trees downstairs was illuminated by the rising sun.
When he pushed the door open and entered the house, a sweet smell filled the living room. Li Dahai was sitting at the dining table reading a newspaper, with a plate of pickles in front of him.
Ye Chen put down his breakfast and was about to ask Niu Lingling to come out for dinner when he heard his mother Niu Lingling's voice coming from the guest room:
"Li Dahai, please call Cheng Pengfei for me quickly and ask him to go to the work unit to register in the morning. Yuan Shanqing has a fever!"
Cheng Pengfei was also unlucky. He had just finished his night shift and was woken up by a phone call from Niu Lingling before he could sleep well. But he didn't dare to complain, especially after learning that the girl was feeling unwell last night.
Ye Chen put the breakfast in his hand on the dining table, walked to the door of the guest room, and asked through the door:
"Mom, does she have a severe fever?"
Niu Lingling's voice came from inside, with a hint of urgency, but not panic:
"It's boiling hot, and it feels like your whole body has been steamed. Li Si, you go to school as soon as you finish eating, and help her get a day off from the teacher. Your dad and I will drive her to the hospital for a check-up."
Ye Chen stood outside the door and paused for a moment, but did not speak immediately. He leaned against the wall in the corridor and thought for a moment - normal reactions after vaccination usually begin six to twelve hours after vaccination, including low fever, fatigue, and redness and swelling at the injection site, which last for about a day and then subside on their own.
As a professional doctor, of course he knew this, but he didn't say it. He knew very well that although Niu Lingling had a son at home, she had always wanted to have a girl at home. After all, she had always been envious of the Cheng family having both children.
